newsitem.title: CANADA: Canada March housing starts fall 0.7 pct.
newsitem.headline: Canada March housing starts fall 0.7 pct.

text.p: Canadian housing starts fell by 0.7 percent in March to a seasonally adjusted annual rate (SAAR) of 158,000 units from 159,100 units (revised up from 158,900) in February, the Canada Mortgage and Housing Corp (CMHC) said on Tuesday.
A Reuter survey of economists had forecast housing starts of 158,000 units.
The federal agency also voiced concern about the effect of mortgage rates. "Market activity remained strong in March.
This pace, however, could slow down as mortgage rates have moved up," said CMHC Senior Economist Michel Laurence.
Actual housing starts rose to 8,208 in March from 7,392 the month before. The SAAR is a monthly figure adjusted to remove normal seasonal variation and multiplied by 12.
